subject: chemistry
title: Collision theory and activation energy
key_idea: Particles react only when they collide with enough energy. That minimum energy is the **activation energy**. Concentration, pressure and surface area raise the frequency of collisions. Temperature raises both the frequency and the energy of collisions.

blocks.text: Collision theory explains why the factors in the previous note change the rate. It has two conditions for a reaction.

items.meaning: Reactions happen only when particles collide with each other and with enough energy.
The minimum energy that particles must have to react.
How many collisions happen per second.

items: The collision must have at least the **activation energy**.
A collision with less than the activation energy does not cause a reaction.
The rate depends on how often particles collide and how many collisions have enough energy.
A reaction needs a collision with at least the activation energy.
More frequent collisions, or more energetic collisions, give a faster rate.

blocks.text: Each factor changes either how often particles collide, or how much energy the collisions have.

rows: More particles in the same volume, closer together
Larger surface area of a solid
More solid particles exposed to the other reactant

blocks.text: Size of pieces and surface area to volume ratio

blocks.label: Surface area to volume ratio
blocks.formula: surface area to volume ratio = surface area ÷ volume

items.text: Surface area = 6 × 1 × 1 = 6 cm². Volume = 1 cm³. The ratio is 6 /cm.
Surface area = 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 cm². Volume = 8 cm³. The ratio is 3 /cm.

diagram.alt: Change the side of a cube to see its surface area, volume and surface area to volume ratio.

items: Smaller pieces have a larger surface area to volume ratio.
More of the solid is exposed to the other reactant, so collisions are more frequent.
Doubling the concentration gives twice as many particles in the same volume, so the frequency of collisions doubles.
Concentration, pressure and surface area change how often particles collide.
Temperature changes the frequency and the energy of collisions.
Smaller pieces have a larger surface area to volume ratio.

sections.heading: Why the rate falls during a reaction

blocks.text: The rate is highest at the start and falls as the reaction goes on.

items: Reactants are used up, so their concentration falls.
There are fewer particles in the same volume, so collisions are less frequent.
The reaction stops when one reactant has been used up.
The rate falls because the concentration of reactants falls.
The reaction stops when a reactant is used up.

checks.q: State what is meant by activation energy.
checks.a: The minimum energy that particles must have to react.

checks.q: Explain why increasing the pressure of a gas increases the rate of reaction.
checks.a: The particles are closer together (more in the same volume), so collisions are more frequent.

checks.q: A cube of side 2 cm is cut into cubes of side 1 cm. Explain why the small cubes react faster.
checks.a: The small cubes have a larger surface area to volume ratio (6 compared with 3), so collisions are more frequent.

exam_phrases: particles have more energy / move faster
more particles have energy greater than the activation energy
there are more particles in the same volume (of solution)
smaller chips have a larger surface area (for the same volume)
fewer particles as the reaction progresses; less frequent collisions

mistakes.wrong: A higher concentration means the particles have more energy.
mistakes.right: Do not say the particles have more energy. Say there are more particles in the same volume, so collisions are more frequent.

mistakes.wrong: Smaller pieces make the particles collide with more energy or at a greater speed.
mistakes.right: Speed and energy of collisions are not accepted for surface area. Say a larger surface area gives more frequent collisions.

mistakes.wrong: A higher concentration gives more collisions.
mistakes.right: More collisions alone is ignored. Say more collisions per unit time, or more frequent collisions.

mistakes.wrong: The rate decreases as the reaction goes on because the particles have less energy.
mistakes.right: An incorrect reference to energy limits the mark. Say there are fewer particles per unit volume, so collisions are less frequent.

worked_example.question:
Temperature also affects the rate of the reaction.

Explain how increasing the temperature affects the rate of the reaction.

You should refer to particles and collisions.
answer_points: Because the particles have more energy (they move faster, or more particles have energy greater than the activation energy).
worked_example.tip: One mark each: the rate, the energy of the particles, and the frequency of collisions.

exam_phrases: more particles present (in the same volume)
more frequent collisions / more chance of collision
particles have more energy so move faster
higher proportion of collisions have at least the activation energy
fewer successful collisions / fewer collisions with activation energy
less frequent collisions as reactants are used up

mistakes.wrong: A higher concentration means more acid is present, so there are more collisions.
mistakes.right: More acid present is ignored, and so is more collisions on its own. Say more particles in the same volume, so more frequent collisions.

mistakes.wrong: At a higher temperature the particles have energy and move fast.
mistakes.right: The answer needs to be comparative: the particles have more energy, so they move faster.

mistakes.wrong: The rate slows as the acid reacts because the reaction stops.
mistakes.right: Reaction stops is ignored. Say the rate decreases as reactants are used up, so collisions are less frequent.

worked_example.question:
An experiment involving an acid was repeated, but with acid of a higher concentration. The rate of reaction was faster.

Explain why the rate of reaction increases when the concentration of acid is increased.
answer_points: There are more particles present in the same volume.
So collisions are more frequent (there is more chance of collision).
worked_example.tip: The two marks are marked independently. Do not refer to energy or particles moving faster.

exam_phrases: more crowded particles / particles are closer together / more particles per unit volume
more collisions per second / collisions more often / increased collision frequency
particles move faster / have more energy
more successful collisions / collisions are more energetic
concentration of reactants decreases / particles become less crowded

mistakes.wrong: A higher concentration means more particles, so more collisions.
mistakes.right: Just more particles and just more collisions are both ignored. Say the particles are more crowded, so there are more collisions per second.

mistakes.wrong: At a higher temperature the particles collide faster.
mistakes.right: Faster collisions is ignored. Say the particles move faster, so collisions are more frequent and more energetic.

mistakes.wrong: As reactants are used up there are fewer particles, so fewer collisions.
mistakes.right: You need the idea of concentration: the concentration of reactants decreases, so there are fewer collisions per second.

worked_example.question:
A student investigates the rate of the reaction between zinc and an excess of hydrochloric acid.

The reaction is faster when more concentrated hydrochloric acid is used.

Explain why.
answer_points: The particles are more crowded (closer together, or more particles per unit volume).
So there are more collisions per second (collisions are more frequent).
worked_example.tip: Just more particles and just more collisions are ignored.
